To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the macronutiens intake and visceral obesity are important factors in blood pressure control.
the macronu-trients composition of diet influences BP in different ways, and this influence is more pronounced in obese patients with Visceral Obesity.

the macronu-trient intake, especially the total calories, carbohydrates, saturated fat and cholesterol, are significantly associated with the blood pressure in obese women with visceral obesity, and that oleic fatty acid is associated with the blood pres-sure in all the obese women.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of macronutrient intake on blood pressure and visceral obesity in obese women.
the relationship between macronutrients and blood pressure in obese women, with and without visceral fat accumulation.
the association between macronutrients and blood pressure in obese women with or without visceral obesity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the higher the intake of saturated fatty acids, the higher the blood pressure in the obese patients with visceral fat, and the higher the intake total protein, animal protein, vegetable protein, linoleic fatty acid, linolenic fatty acid, and oleic fatty acid, the lower the blood pressure in obese patients with and without visceral fat.

the higher total calories, carbohydrate and fat intake, and the higher intake of saturated fatty acids and the lower intake of oleic fatty acids, are positively correlated with blood pressure in obese women, especially in those with visceral obesity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a low fat diet with high content of unsaturated fatty acids is recommended for obese patients with visceral fat.
the higher the intake of total calories and total fat, the higher the blood pressure.
the higher intake of saturated fat and cholesterol in the diet of obese women with visceral obesity may be associated with the increase of blood pressure.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the intake of saturated fats, cholesterol and carbohydrate is associated with higher blood pressure, whereas the intake of unsaturated fats, especially linoleic fatty acid is associated with lower blood pressure.
the macronutrients composition of the diet is an important factor that influences blood pressure in obese patients with Visceral obesity.
the intake of total fat, saturated fat, and cholesterol should be limited in obese patients, especially in those with visceral obesity.
